label: weak: copy-phase input z (also n/e/g) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phases), and only on steps that re-input a token that already appeared (in_first=0). It fires mostly in long sequences (L=9 holds 69% of activation mass) and early-middle in recall (recall_idx 3 holds 48%, to_go 5 holds 39%; t=12 is the peak). The input token is z far more than any other (12.5x lift, 45% of mass); n, e, g and 3 come next. The strongest activations are copy-phase z at recall_idx 3 when L=9. But it is very sparse and unselective: even copy-phase z with L>=8 is active only about 12% of the time (dev F1 0.17). Widening to z/n/e/g raises mass recall to 0.73 but drops precision to 6%. No predicate tried reached useful precision, so this is a statistical tendency, not an explanation.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: z, n, g, e; t=11: z, n, g, e; t=13: z, n, g, e) and the token being output (most: 3, l, h, b, z, v; least: p, o, d, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=9 & t=12, recall_idx=3.
